text: Write the ending of a story called The Finishing Line, about a race that someone has spent a long
time preparing for. In your writing, create a sense of drama and atmosphere.
Write two contrasting pieces (300–450 words each) about a famous building or monument, the
first from the perspective of a tourist visiting the site for the first time, and the second from the
perspective of a local person going past it on their way to work. In your writing, create a sense of
atmosphere and place.
Write a descriptive piece about a campsite during an expedition. In your writing, focus on the
colours, sounds and movements at the campsite to help your reader imagine the scene.
Section B: Writing for an audience
A new shopping centre recently opened in your town. Write a review of the shopping centre, which
will be published in your local newspaper.
Students from your school recently did a week’s work experience, working in local businesses.
Your head teacher has asked for some feedback. Write two contrasting letters to the head teacher
(300–450 words each), one from a student who gained from the experience, and another from a
student who did not consider it a good use of school time.
Write the script of a voiceover for a TV documentary about popular childhood games. The
programme is aimed at a range of ages, and aims to show how games have changed over the
years. In your writing, create a sense of interest and enthusiasm.
